sk-e617e04f.stem: In which part of which bone is the inner ear located?
sk-e617e04f.explanation: The petrous part (pyramid) is the hardest bone in the body; it contains the cochlea, vestibule and semicircular canals. The middle ear cavity also lies between the petrous and tympanic parts.

sk-1864ac93.stem: Which fontanelle closes last in infants, and at about what age?
sk-1864ac93.explanation: The anterior fontanelle (the diamond-shaped opening at the bregma) is the largest and closes last (around 18–24 months). The posterior fontanelle closes at 2–3 months, the sphenoidal at about 6 months, the mastoid at 6–18 months. A sunken anterior fontanelle suggests dehydration, a bulging one raised intracranial pressure.

sk-2a63ac57.stem: The bregma is the meeting point of which sutures?
sk-2a63ac57.explanation: The bregma, the site of the anterior fontanelle, is where the coronal and sagittal sutures meet. The lambda is where the sagittal and lambdoid sutures meet, the site of the posterior fontanelle.

sk-2fcb0376.stem: After being hit in the face by a tennis ball, a patient has double vision on looking up, a sunken eyeball and numbness of the cheek and upper lip on the same side. What is the most likely fracture?
sk-2fcb0376.explanation: In blunt orbital trauma the pressure breaks out through one of the weakest walls, the floor (maxilla). Inferior rectus and fat are trapped in the maxillary sinus and upward gaze is restricted. Injury to the infraorbital nerve in the groove/canal of the floor causes sensory loss of the cheek, lower lid and upper lip. The medial wall (orbital plate of the ethmoid) is the thinnest and also fractures often.

sk-b4b77595.stem: Which structures form the bony part of the nasal septum?
options: Frontal process of the maxilla and nasal bone
Inferior nasal concha and palatine bone
Vomer and perpendicular plate of the ethmoid
sk-b4b77595.explanation: The nasal septum is formed posteroinferiorly by the vomer, posterosuperiorly by the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid and anteriorly by the septal cartilage. A deviated septum is usually at the cartilage–bone junction.

sk-9a7db56f.stem: Which of the following is a separate bone, not part of the ethmoid?
sk-9a7db56f.explanation: The superior and middle conchae extend from the labyrinth of the ethmoid. The inferior concha is a facial bone in its own right and articulates with the maxilla, lacrimal, palatine and ethmoid bones.

sk-e474b6d7.stem: Which bone forms the posterior quarter of the hard palate?
sk-e474b6d7.explanation: The anterior three quarters of the hard palate are formed by the palatine processes of the maxillae, the posterior quarter by the horizontal plates of the palatine bones. Their junction is the transverse palatine suture.

sk-a81fa9ba.stem: Which bones form the fossa for the lacrimal sac?
options: Lacrimal bone and the frontal process of the maxilla
sk-a81fa9ba.explanation: The lacrimal sac sits in the fossa for the lacrimal sac at the front of the medial orbital wall. The fossa is formed in front by the frontal process of the maxilla (anterior lacrimal crest) and behind by the lacrimal bone (posterior lacrimal crest). Below, the sac opens into the inferior meatus through the nasolacrimal duct.

sk-8a17fa1f.stem: The zygomatic arch is formed by the union of which structures?
options: Frontal process of the zygomatic bone and frontal bone
Greater wing of the sphenoid and temporal bone
Mastoid process of the temporal bone and zygomatic bone
Temporal process of the zygomatic bone and zygomatic process of the temporal bone
Zygomatic process of the maxilla and sphenoid
sk-8a17fa1f.explanation: The zygomatic arch is formed in front by the temporal process of the zygomatic bone and behind by the zygomatic process of the temporal bone. Masseter arises from its lower border; the tendon of temporalis passes beneath the arch to the coronoid process.

sk-5ff889bf.stem: The occipital condyles articulate with which bone?
sk-5ff889bf.explanation: The occipital condyles form the atlanto-occipital joint with the upper surfaces of the lateral masses of the atlas. The 'yes' nodding movement (flexion–extension) occurs at this joint; the 'no' movement occurs at the atlanto-axial joint.

sk-d3f9241b.stem: Which nerve passes through the supraorbital foramen, and from which main nerve does it come?
sk-d3f9241b.explanation: The supraorbital nerve, a branch of the frontal nerve, emerges through the supraorbital foramen (notch) of the frontal bone and supplies the forehead and front of the scalp. This point is examined as the V1 pressure point in trigeminal neuralgia.

sk-95627bc6.stem: How many permanent teeth and how many deciduous (milk) teeth are there, respectively?
sk-95627bc6.explanation: Each half-jaw in the permanent dentition has 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars and 3 molars (32 in all); the deciduous dentition has 2 incisors, 1 canine and 2 molars (20 in all). There are no premolars among the milk teeth.

sk-e0da37ac.stem: Where does the base (footplate) of the stapes sit?
sk-e0da37ac.explanation: The footplate of the stapes is held in the oval window on the medial wall of the middle ear by the annular ligament and transmits vibration to the perilymph. In otosclerosis new bone here fixes the stapes and causes conductive hearing loss. The round window is closed by the secondary tympanic membrane.

sk-11bbc925.stem: Which vertebra has no vertebral body?
sk-11bbc925.explanation: During development the body of the atlas joins the axis to form the dens. The atlas is a ring made of anterior and posterior arches and two lateral masses; instead of a spinous process it carries a posterior tubercle.
